outline.chapter_title: The Role of Attention and Why It’s a Bottleneck
outline.description: Introduce the Transformer attention mechanism, its quadratic scaling challenge, and why optimizing exact attention matters for long-context and multimodal applications.
subtopics: Self-attention basics and quadratic scaling with sequence length
Impact on long-context tasks: documents, codebases, images, audio, video
Exact vs. approximate attention: trade-offs and when exact attention is needed
From algorithm design to hardware-aware implementations

outline.description: Explain standard GPU attention and how FlashAttention/FlashAttention-2 reduce memory traffic by kernel fusion and tiling while maintaining exactness.
subtopics: Standard attention: computing S=QK^T, P=softmax(S), O=PV
Numerical stability of softmax: rowmax subtraction and FP32 accumulation
FlashAttention v1: IO-aware tiling and fused kernels to avoid HBM intermediates
FlashAttention-2: parallelization over sequence length and improved occupancy
Limitations of FA-2 on Hopper (H100): 35% utilization vs GEMM 80–90%

outline.description: Provide the hardware background needed to understand FlashAttention-3’s design on NVIDIA Hopper (H100).
subtopics: Memory hierarchy: GMEM/HBM, L2, SMEM, registers; bandwidth vs capacity
Thread hierarchy: threads, warps, warpgroups, CTAs, clusters, grids
Asynchrony: Tensor Memory Accelerator (TMA) and asynchronous WGMMA
Warp-specialization and register reallocation (setmaxnreg)
Low-precision accelerators: FP16/BF16 vs FP8 throughput and constraints

outline.chapter_title: Mathematics of Attention and Its Gradients
outline.description: Review the forward and backward computations of attention to motivate what must be fused, tiled, and overlapped.
subtopics: Forward: S=αQK^T, P=softmax(S), O=PV; local softmax accumulation logic
Backward: dV=P^T dO, dP=dO V^T, dS=dsoftmax(dP), dQ=α dS K, dK=α dS^T Q
Stable streaming softmax: maintaining running max m and sum ℓ
Implications for kernel fusion and memory reuse

outline.description: Present the three core ideas that make FA-3 faster and more accurate on Hopper: producer–consumer asynchrony, overlapping softmax with GEMMs, and FP8 with accuracy-preserving quantization.
subtopics: Producer–consumer asynchrony with warp-specialization
Interleaving block-wise matmul and softmax within and across warpgroups
FP8 acceleration: layout constraints, block quantization, incoherent processing
Performance and accuracy goals: 1.5–2.0x speedup FP16, ~1.2 PFLOPs FP8, reduced FP8 error

outline.chapter_title: Producer–Consumer Asynchrony: Warp-Specialization and Ping-Pong Scheduling
outline.description: Detail the CTA-level algorithm using TMA and WGMMA with circular SMEM buffers, and how ping-pong scheduling overlaps softmax with GEMMs across warpgroups.
subtopics: CTA view: tiles of Q (rows) and streaming K/V (columns) with circular SMEM buffer
Producer warpgroup: TMA loads for Q, then pipelined K/V blocks
Consumer warpgroup: WGMMA for QK^T and PV with local softmax rescaling
Ping-pong scheduling with barriers: staggering GEMM0 and GEMM1 across warpgroups
Throughput intuition: MFU exponentials vs Tensor Cores and why overlap helps
Applying to MQA/GQA by indexing without duplicating K/V

outline.description: Explain how FA-3 breaks strict iteration dependencies to overlap softmax of one block with GEMMs of adjacent blocks within the same warpgroup.
subtopics: Dependency challenge: softmax depends on QK^T; PV depends on softmax
Two-stage pipeline: S_cur, P̃_cur, PV(prev) overlapped with computing S_next
Asynchronous WGMMA: commit without wait; targeted waits to stage transitions
Register and buffer management: extra S_next and P̃ buffers
Compiler reordering considerations and verifying overlapped SASS
Trade-offs: register pressure, tile sizes, potential 3-stage extension

outline.chapter_title: FP8 FlashAttention-3: Layouts, Transposes, and Operand Conformance
outline.description: Cover the engineering needed to exploit FP8 Tensor Cores while maintaining the fused pipeline: operand layout rules, in-kernel transposes, and accumulator reformatting.
subtopics: FP8 WGMMA k-major constraint vs typical head-major tensors
Why pre-transpose in GMEM is undesirable for bandwidth-limited workloads
In-kernel transpose of V tiles using LDSM/STSM (ldmatrix/stmatrix) with packed bytes
Scheduling the V transpose under GEMM shadow to hide its cost
FP8 accumulator vs operand layout mismatch and byte-permute solution
Coordinating P-tile column permutation with V-tile row permutation for correctness

outline.chapter_title: FP8 Accuracy: Block Quantization and Incoherent Processing
outline.description: Explain FA-3’s accuracy techniques that cut FP8 error despite outliers in large models, and how they integrate seamlessly with the tiled algorithm.
subtopics: FP8 (e4m3) constraints: 3-bit mantissa, 4-bit exponent; sensitivity to outliers
Per-tensor scaling baseline and its limitations
Block quantization: per-block scales for Q, K, V aligned to algorithm tiles
Incoherent processing: orthogonal randomization (Hadamard + sign flips)
Complexity and fusion: O(d log d) transforms fused with rotary embedding
Overall effect: up to 2.6x RMSE reduction vs per-tensor FP8 baseline

outline.chapter_title: Algorithm Walkthrough: Forward and Backward FA-3
outline.description: Walk through the complete kernel flow with FP16 and FP8 variants, including the softmax streaming state and epilogue writes; outline the backward pass adaptations.
subtopics: Forward FP16: producer–consumer flow, two-stage overlap, local softmax, epilogue
Forward FP8: added in-kernel V transpose and accumulator reformat steps
State maintenance: running m_i, ℓ_i, and rescaling of O_i
Backward pass sketch: recomputation strategy and where overlap applies
Causal masking considerations and performance impact

outline.description: Provide practical guidance on building FA-3 kernels using CUTLASS-like primitives, managing resources, and validating pipeline overlap.
subtopics: Using CUTLASS abstractions for TMA and WGMMA on Hopper
Circular SMEM buffer depth s and its interaction with pipeline stages
Register allocation with setmaxnreg and balancing producer/consumer warps
Tile size choices (Br, Bc, d) vs register pressure and occupancy
Barrier placement and verifying overlap in SASS
Integrating with frameworks and fusing pre/post ops (rotary, quantization)

outline.description: Summarize benchmarks and ablations showing FA-3’s speedups over FA-2 and standard attention, and accuracy gains for FP8.
subtopics: Throughput: FP16 up to 740 TFLOPs/s (75% utilization), FP8 near 1.2 PFLOPs/s
Forward/backward speedups vs FlashAttention-2 and PyTorch standard
Comparisons with vendor libraries (cuDNN) under various head dims and masks
Ablations: effect of warp-specialization and 2-stage pipelining
RMSE evaluations vs FP64 reference with synthetic outliers
When FP8 leads or lags: head dim and causal masking effects

outline.description: Discuss open engineering and research directions inspired by FA-3, portability, and broader implications for long-context models.
subtopics: Inference-specific optimizations and persistent-kernel design for FP8
Load balancing for small sequences and causal masking
Training stability and convergence with FP8 attention at scale
Applicability to other accelerators beyond Hopper
Potential 3-stage pipelines and deeper fusion with surrounding layers
Open-source availability and integration plans (PyTorch, Hugging Face)
